title: OpalGrid x Redwood - Partner Discovery
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and OpalGrid. Discussed potential reseller/integration partnership, OpalGrid's GPU-enabled cloud offering, joint go-to-market, technical integration points (VPC peering, private deployment, dedicated capacity), and pilot/benchmark plan. Security and compliance requirements (SOC2, KMS, audit logs) were flagged. Agreed next steps for technical deep dive and shared docs.
next_steps: Maya to send partner deck, pricing matrix, and Redwood one-pager (by 2026-02-20)
Alex and Priya to schedule technical deep dive to map network/topology (week of 2026-02-23)
OpalGrid to share sample workload characteristics and expected QPS for pilot (by 2026-02-24)
Tina and Redwood security team to exchange SOC2 report and KMS architecture doc (by 2026-02-27)
Schedule joint benchmark run on OpalGrid infra with a 7B model (proposed week of 2026-03-02)
action_items: Maya Patel | Send partner deck + pricing matrix | 2026-02-20
Alex Chen | Prepare network/integration checklist and Redwood private deployment notes | 2026-02-23
Priya Nair | Provide sample workloads, peak tokens/min, and storage details | 2026-02-24
Tina Gomez | Share SOC2 cert and list of required contractual clauses | 2026-02-27
Leo Martinez | Draft commercial partnership outline (reseller vs referral) | 2026-03-01
transcript:
00:00:12 Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on the partnership side. We also have Alex our SE and Jordan from solutions. Quick intros?
00:00:25 Samir (OpalGrid): Samir here, head of infra at OpalGrid. Priya is our cloud architect and Leo runs partnerships. Tina from security is on as well.
00:00:38 Alex (SE): Great to meet you all. We'll keep this high level then dig into any technical bits.
00:01:10 Maya: The goal today is to understand OpalGrid's offering and see where Redwood fits — whether resale, integration for private deployments, or joint go-to-market. I'll hand to Samir to give a quick overview.
00:01:28 Samir: Sure. OpalGrid is a regional cloud with GPU pools, we focus on latency-sensitive inference workloads, we have both shared and dedicated pools, private tenancy options, and some customers that need on-prem interconnect. We're looking for an inference partner to offer managed LLM endpoints to customers without them building the ops layer.
00:01:55 Priya: A couple details — our infra is multi-region within NA and EU, we use VPCs with optional direct connect, and we have NVLink-backed nodes (A100/Tesla-like, also newer Ada-type GPUs). We typically offer reserved capacity for enterprise customers.
00:02:12 Jordan (Solutions): Sounds aligned. Redwood supports hosted, dedicated, and private deployment models — same API across them. For partner integrations we often do either: 1) resale where you surface Redwood hosted API to your customers, 2) joint private deployments where Redwood control plane runs in our cloud and we manage inference on your GPU pools, or 3) a self-hosted package for air-gapped regulated clients.
00:02:45 Leo (Partnerships): From a go-to-market lens, we're interested in reseller and also a co-sell where we can pitch integrated stacks to ISVs. We do have some customers asking specifically for SOC2 and KMS integration.
00:03:05 Tina (Security): Yes, security first. We need to understand encryption at rest, KMS integrations, audit logs retention, and MFA/SSO for tenant access. Can you outline Redwood's typical security posture?
00:03:22 Maya: Absolutely. Redwood has SOC2, we support customer-managed KMS for private deployments, and we surface audit logs via our console. For dedicated pools we can offer strict network isolation and RBAC. We'll share the SOC2 report and an architecture note after this call.
00:03:45 Priya: On the technical side, we'll need to see how K/V cache and batching interacts with our networking. Does Redwood require open outbound connectivity or can it work over VPC peering and private VPC endpoints?
00:04:05 Alex: Good question. For Private we offer a control plane that can be in your VPC and we use private endpoints — no public egress required for inference. There are some webhook callbacks/etc that need routing, but we can run them over peered networks. For dedicated we can also route calls locally with a small egress for control signals.
00:04:35 Samir: Latency is critical for some of our telco customers — sub-50ms token latency on small models matters. How does Redwood handle tail latency and batching?
00:04:48 Jordan: Our runtime supports continuous batching and smart routing to keep p99 latency down while optimizing cost. For extreme low-latency use cases we recommend dedicated pinned capacity and smaller batch windows, plus local KV cache pinned to the serving nodes. We can run a benchmark to validate.
00:05:12 Priya: Okay, benchmarks are key. We want to see throughput/cost tradeoffs across different model sizes. Also curious about quantization support — can you run int8/4bit to increase density?
00:05:27 Alex: Yes, we support quantized model variants; runtime picks kernels and quant paths based on perf profiles. We can recommend quantization/instancing profiles based on your workload. For some models we've found 4-bit + calibration keeps quality acceptable and improves density a ton.
00:05:50 Leo: Commercial question — do you like to sell via uplift or do you do revenue share for partners? What's typical?
00:05:58 Maya: We have multiple models. For reseller we do listed pricing with partner uplift and enable a resale contract. For tight integrations and enterprise deals we can do revenue share or referral. We'll pass the partner pricing and a proposal template.
00:06:18 Tina: On compliance: our customers ask for data residency, audit trails, and ability to do customer-managed encryption. How is data retained in hosted mode?
00:06:28 Maya: Hosted API stores minimal logs for billing/trace; customers can opt out of retention. For regulated customers we push private deployment or dedicated where data never leaves customer network and audit logs are delivered to your SIEM.
00:06:45 Samir: One technical constraint — some of our customers need offline/on-prem options behind strict firewall. How heavy is Redwood's on-prem package?
00:06:56 Alex: We have an on-prem package that can be air-gapped; it requires a small control plane deploy or a support contract for update channels. It includes our inference runtime and orchestration. It's heavier to manage but doable for big enterprise.
00:07:15 Priya: Great. For the pilot: what do you need from us to scope it?
00:07:22 Jordan: Ideally: sample prompt sets, expected QPS and concurrency, model family you want to test, and whether you want latency first or cost-first configs. We'll propose a 2-week pilot with benchmarks on a representative model (say 7B) across shared vs dedicated pools.
00:07:44 Priya: We can provide that. We'll also need an NDA and partner agreement for joint marketing.
00:07:51 Maya: We'll follow up with the partner NDA and deck.
00:08:02 Leo: Any blockers on the technical side for integration? Network ports, certs, etc?
00:08:09 Alex: Mostly peering and private endpoints; certs for mutual TLS for inter-service calls; we can provide a network checklist. We might ask for ephemeral capacity for benchmark runs.
00:08:28 Samir: Cost question: customers often ask can you run cheaper with batching and caching? Can Redwood share typical cost-per-token numbers on different configs?
00:08:40 Maya: We can share cost ranges; Redwood Optimize offers recommendations and we can run a profile on your workloads to estimate unit economics. We'll include rough numbers in the partner deck.
00:09:05 Tina: Also need to confirm SLAs for dedicated pools — uptime and latency SLOs.
00:09:12 Maya: For Dedicated we offer SLA-backed uptime and define latency targets per-contract. We'll include example SLA language.
00:09:25 Priya: One more: orchestration — do you support autoscaling policies and burst capacity in the dedicated model?
00:09:33 Alex: Yes, configurable autoscaling policies and burst capacity windows are supported; you can configure thresholds by tail latency or CPU/GPU util.
00:09:48 Leo: From partnerships POV, we want co-branded collateral and perhaps a launch webinar.
00:09:55 Maya: Happy to co-host a webinar. We'll put together a joint launch plan after pilot success.
00:10:12 Samir: Sounds good. Any outstanding technical risks you foresee?
00:10:18 Jordan: Mostly integration checklist items: KMS handshake, VPC peering, cert management, and throughput testing. None are blockers.
00:10:30 Maya: To be concrete, we'll send the partner deck, the partner pricing matrix, the SOC2 and KMS notes, and Alex will follow up on a technical deep dive.
00:10:42 Priya: We'll send sample workloads and a list of customer compliance asks.
00:11:00 Maya: Cool. Shall we agree on target dates — technical deep dive week of Feb 23, benchmark week of March 2?
00:11:10 Leo: That works for us.
00:11:16 Tina: We'll try to get SOC2 materials over by Feb 27.
00:11:23 Samir: Anything else on commercial terms? We should loop in legal early for reseller language.
00:11:30 Maya: Agreed — I'll introduce our partnerships legal contact in the follow up.
00:11:40 Jordan: Quick note — for the benchmark we recommend a 7B and a 13B run to show scaling characteristics; we'll bring perf scripts.
00:11:50 Priya: Good. Also curious if Redwood supports multi-tenant isolation in a single node via CUDA multi-instance or is it strictly per-instance?
00:12:02 Alex: We do both patterns depending on model and isolation needs; for highest isolation we pin model instances to nodes. For density we use multi-instance but only with tenant-level cryptographic isolation.
00:12:20 Maya: Okay, we'll wrap. Thanks everyone for time. We'll email the deck and docs by Friday.
00:12:30 Samir: Thanks, talk soon.
00:12:35 Maya: Bye all.
notes: OpalGrid wants reseller + co-sell; interested in private deployments and dedicated capacity
Security checklist required: SOC2, KMS, audit logs, RBAC
Pilot to benchmark 7B model on OpalGrid infra week of 2026-03-02
Commercial models to evaluate: reseller uplift vs revenue share
